source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Thresholded AIPW is analyzed for asymptotic normality and Wald inference under weak overlap and nuisance-rate conditions.
The article studies IPW with small denominators and trimming, including robustness across asymptotic distributions.
The paper establishes minimax rates for Hölder-smooth CATE and uses localized fuzzy hypotheses for its lower bound.
The paper links unbounded inverse weights and relative support tails to irregular, slower-than-parametric estimation, including an exogenous-selection treatment-effect example.
The article attributes limited-overlap CI distortion to small local sample sizes and constructs small-sample-based robust intervals.
The paper identifies distribution shift with weak overlap as an important extension beyond its i.i.d. structure-agnostic lower-bound framework.

This unpublished but archival preprint develops bias-corrected DR estimators robust to weak overlap while retaining original causal targets; it does not itself establish the proposal's minimax frontier.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a primitive arm-potential integrability condition, such as a uniform E|Y1| envelope or a compatible weighted outcome-regression condition, then rederive every upper and lower rate channel on that repaired class rather than assuming the ATE exists implicitly.
Add MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 to related work and state precisely why its bias-corrected trimmed DR estimator does not subsume a minimax public-function risk or honest-length frontier.

After repairing the model, state whether the added integrability restriction changes the least-favourable shell constructions; if it does, replace the four-channel equality with the rate actually attainable on the integrable class.

recommended_next_step: Revise the law class to make the full-population ATE finite and revalidate the four-channel frontier on that class, while adding the omitted 2026 weak-overlap DR comparator.
